Main decisions:
- All material numbers live in one GDScript const table, world/items/matter_cards.gd. It has 58 cards: the design's 52 entries, with steel and plastic each split in two, plus today's sequoia, larch, aspen and cedar. Numbers are in SI. The order of the cards is fixed and only grows, so a card's position can be sent over the network as a number. matter.gd becomes the API over that table.
- Today's numbers are copied exactly. For pine to cedar, the volume price is 3 x cut / 0.6. For the three stones, hardness is 3 x UCS, the volume price is hardness / 0.8, and the crack price is computed from the old K and E values (granite comes out at 144.8177 J/m², as now). Soil keeps 4e4 and 8e3 J/m³. A guard test checks all of this.
- There is one function for every blow, Impact.blow(tool, mat, e, ctx). It also has a general gate, which is today's rock_eff formula. The tool's brittle loss only applies on materials from 100 MPa up, so wood and soil come out at share 1 and do not change. As today, the stone crack is paid from 0.1 of the blow on top of the crushed volume (it is not taken out of it), which keeps W1 bit-for-bit.
- Wood, stone and soil switch to it with small edits: one line in AxeSwing.plan, plus Impact.rock, Impact.soil, RockNode and Spall. The copied constants are deleted.
- W1 starts by recording a fresh baseline on a main that already has tasks 58 and 59. This matters because 207 cm³ may have moved after task 58. After W1, the numbers runs, the task 58 regression battery, the tech test, impact_test and dig_test must give identical results.

What each later wave adds:
- W2: water pools with an integer litre count, and a bucket. Glass, ice, ceramic and porcelain shatter on the stone canvas into at most 40 Voronoi shards (no CSG), and the shards become items. Drop and throw impacts are measured on every body, but only fragile things break; the rest just make a thud. Tool wear uses Archard, sharpening is the T key on sandstone, and it is tuned so a steel axe dulls after about 1950 blows on pine. Sand, gravel, clay, mud and snow get their own material per ground node. Late joiners get a replay of what the range spawned.
- W3: the sheet class, a 5 mm byte bitmap with integer cut-line events, a new knife, and strips as items.
- W4: metal plates with a 1 cm dent field, through-cuts, bending at yield, and an element system with heat only (forge).
- W5: fire, water, frost, rust and melting as 3 rules, ticked 4 times a second, with at most 16 fires.

Every wave lists its parts with owner files (no file owned twice in a wave), new files, tests, perf budgets, risks, days and model.
